extracted.intended_audience: institutional investors, proxy voting analysts, and corporate governance professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and decision‑making guidance used by institutional investors to evaluate portfolio companies (boards, executive pay, risk oversight, and shareholder proposals) and to inform proxy votes and engagement outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board composition and effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek to understand to what extent board members, who are elected to represent the interests of all shareholders, are suitably independent, capable, and experienced to carry out their duties. We also aim to understand how boards assess and enhance their own effectiveness over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the board documents an 'ideal board composition' (mix of independence, skills, diversity, experience). Compare candidate slates to that profile (e.g., Assicurazioni Generali case). Support slates that best align with the published profile and that include a majority of independent directors. Consider board refreshment where prior governance incidents occurred (e.g., WiseTech). Use market-specific governance frameworks when assessing appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director capacity and commitments (overboarding)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the number of directorships and external commitments held by an individual allows them sufficient time and attention to effectively fulfill their responsibilities; excessive outside roles can make a director 'overboarded.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess capacity case-by-case, reviewing disclosed outside roles, meeting attendance, and any changes in responsibilities (examples: Ecolab, Netflix). When boards under common control are involved, consider whether overlapping responsibilities mitigate concerns about excessive commitments. Look for clear disclosure of individual commitments and board policies addressing director commitments; poor attendance or unexplained absences can justify withholding support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material weaknesses and audit committee oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: When companies disclose consecutive years of material weakness in financial reporting, assess the magnitude/severity and remediation efforts and look to the audit committee to disclose actions taken to oversee and mitigate risks to shareholder returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze remediation plans, timelines, audit committee evolution, auditor assessments, and increased disclosure (Evolv example). Expanded and detailed remediation timelines and disclosure demonstrating proactive oversight support votes for auditors and audit committee members. Lack of remediation detail is a concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director independence (market-specific compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Look for boards of non-controlled companies to be majority independent and evaluate board composition against relevant market-specific governance frameworks (e.g., South Korean Commercial Code).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review public disclosures, proxy statements, and corporate websites for independence classifications. Engage companies to clarify discrepancies and request updated disclosures (Hanwha Ocean, NBK). Support/review elections based on whether disclosed independence meets legal/market thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of board Chair and CEO — contextual evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not advocate for a single board structure by default; assess whether combined Chair/CEO role is effectively counterbalanced and whether governance structures provide independent oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate presence and defined responsibilities of a lead independent director, bylaws and governance structures (annual elections, majority voting, shareholder thresholds), committee independence, board accessibility, and any identified concerns about independence or effectiveness (Lincoln National example). If counterbalances and independence are strong, may not support mandatory separation proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board diversity disclosure and comply-or-explain obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess board diversity (e.g., gender diversity) and whether companies comply with or adequately explain departures from market diversity targets and listing-rule expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under jurisdictions with 'comply or explain' requirements (U.K. Listing Rules), expect disclosure acknowledging diversity targets and plans to address gaps. Lack of disclosure or low representation (example: 14% female directors) can justify voting against key directors (chair) to signal concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board structure choice (one-tier vs two-tier) — evaluate rationale and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards are generally best placed to determine their optimal structure; evaluation should focus on the rationale for change and the resulting level of independence and oversight rather than imposing a preferred structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the change increases independence or strengthens monitoring (Toyota example: transition to one-tier with audit committee, reduction of executive directors, increase in independent nonexecutives). Support when resulting independence meets stated policy thresholds and rationale is compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight of strategy and material risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Boards should be meaningfully involved in formation, evolution, and oversight of company strategy and should have ongoing oversight of material risks and mitigation plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage to understand board involvement in strategy, how material risks are identified/governed/disclosed, and whether oversight processes (committees, reporting cadence) are robust. Use findings to inform voting and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight of employee health and safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect boards to oversee risks related to employee health and safety and to implement remedial actions when oversight deficiencies are identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for concrete remediation steps, introduction of Three Lines model or similar risk frameworks, restructuring for clearer accountability (e.g., making a division an autonomous entity with independent directors), and implementation of support mechanisms (hotlines, surveys). Adequate remediation and enhanced oversight can justify support for board recommendations (Hankyu Hanshin).

rubrics_metrics.name: Board oversight of human rights and supply chain risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess board-level processes for overseeing human rights risks, due diligence approaches, supplier mapping, investigations of allegations, and independent audit results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage with independent directors and management to review human rights due diligence, remedial actions, mapping of supply chain risks, and outcomes of independent audits; satisfactory explanations and audit findings that mitigate concerns support votes and indicate better oversight (Zhen Ding, JSW examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Shareholder engagement formats and access (hybrid meetings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid annual general meetings enhance accessibility and investor participation and can support effective exercise of shareholder rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note whether companies provide hybrid formats that allow in-person and virtual participation; consider high levels of engagement with independent directors (Australia & New Zealand example) as positive for governance and investor access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach to shareholder proposals — relevance, duplication, and investor role
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating shareholder proposals, assess whether the requested information or action is already publicly disclosed and whether the proposal seeks to influence company strategy/operations; passive investors may abstain on proposals that effectively ask investors to opine on strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosures already address the proposal's request (e.g., Apple’s responsible AI disclosures), do not support. For proposals seeking strategic or operational direction (e.g., certain climate or human-capital operational asks), consider abstaining in line with passive investor orientation (Aviva, Rio Tinto, M&S). Engage beforehand to determine if additional disclosure or clarification suffices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger and acquisition evaluation — governance-centric lens
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating M&A transactions, assess whether a transaction is likely to create long-term returns using a governance-centric lens focused on valuation, rationale, board oversight of the process, and the governance profile of the combined entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the solicitation process, whether a strategic transaction committee oversaw the deal, valuation metrics, strategic rationale (scale, access to capital), and expected governance improvements in the surviving entity. Support transactions that demonstrably improve long-term shareholder returns and governance (Enterprise Bancorp example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Severance and transaction-related pay arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess severance arrangements linked to transactions for alignment with long-term shareholder returns; oppose arrangements that include substantial single-trigger cash payments automatically payable on deal completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject severance packages judged misaligned with long-term interests (Pacific Premier example). Focus on trigger design (single vs. double-trigger), quantum, and alignment with shareholder outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive pay — alignment with long-term shareholder returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound pay policies and practices should be linked to long-term relative company performance and drive long-term shareholder returns. Expect clear disclosure of compensation policies, board oversight, and alignment with shareholders’ long-term returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the rationale for proposed changes, benchmarking processes, alignment with strategy, use of rigorous performance-based targets, and detailed disclosure (GSK example). Consider plan structure (short- vs long-term incentives), vesting schedules, and whether performance metrics are rigorous and quantifiable (Fox Factory example). Scrutinize one-time awards for rationale, structure, size, and link to long-term performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for equity awards over cash replacements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer executives be awarded equity rather than cash, because cash awards typically do not align executive pay with shareholder returns; oppose situations where shareholders face a 'false choice' between approving equity awards or accepting an automatic cash replacement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage companies where equity awards may be replaced with cash if not approved; emphasize importance of governance structures that allow shareholders to exercise rights effectively and align pay practices with long-term shareholder returns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to vote against remuneration reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary reasons to vote against a remuneration report include lack of disclosure preventing assessment of robustness/appropriateness of variable pay awards and use of metrics that are not quantifiable or lack sufficient rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review disclosure on variable pay awards and metrics; withhold support if insufficiently disclosed or if metrics are vague/unquantifiable. Engage to request improved disclosure and measurable targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case-by-case assessment for global or regionally-differentiated remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: For companies with global operations or secondary listings citing significant remuneration packages as necessary to attract/retain management in regions with different pay practices, assess plans on a case-by-case basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support proposals only after determining that structure is appropriate, potential overall remuneration serves shareholders' interests, and adequate disclosure and measurable performance targets are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for auditors and audit committee members when remediation and disclosure improve
rubrics_metrics.description: Where company disclosures and remediation plans become more detailed and thorough over time—demonstrating proactive approaches—the funds may support the auditor and audit committee despite previous material weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for expanded disclosure, detailed remediation timelines, and clearer accounts of board/audit committee/auditor activities over prior periods (Evolv example). Improved transparency and evidence of remediation justify continued support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of 'Say on Climate' and climate-related votes
rubrics_metrics.description: When companies put forward votes on climate-related financial disclosures or 'Say on Climate' proposals, evaluate the clarity of regulatory framework, existing disclosures, board oversight processes, expertise at board level, and whether the proposal seeks ratification of operational/capital allocation matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the absence of a clear regulatory framework, passive investors may abstain (Aviva, Rio Tinto). If disclosures and board oversight are robust and aligned with standards such as TCFD, and the proposal does not ask shareholders to approve operational decisions, this informs support/abstention decisions. Carefully analyze the proposal language to identify requests that go beyond disclosure.
